Subject: Wintergreen DPA: conditional egress/playbook questions

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and security teams reviewed the DPA draft and had a couple of pull-through questions we'd like to resolve before signature. High level asks:

1) Conditional/transient cross-region processing: we need a short written playbook describing the exact conditions under which data may be routed outside of the US (failover, capacity burst, operational debugging), the maximum time window, and notification commitments.

2) Subprocessor roster + evidence: we need an up-to-date list of subprocessors that could receive transient traffic (analytics, telemetry, monitoring) and their locales.

3) DPA redlines: attached is a consolidated set of comments from legal (DPA_redline_comments.xlsx). We flagged the transient-egress clause and the SLA wording around notification.

Can Redwood provide a one-page playbook and confirm whether you can commit to a 48-hour maximum for transient failover (Wintergreen requirement)? If 48h is not feasible, please propose the shortest supported window and any options (e.g., Dedicated or Private deployments).

Also copying our procurement lead (Matt) to coordinate DocuSign timeline.

Thanks — would prefer answers in writing first; we can follow with a short call if helpful.

Best,
Asha Rao
Head of Privacy & Risk
Wintergreen Health

Attachments: DPA_redline_comments.xlsx (spreadsheet of clause-level comments)

Eve / Marissa — quick technical note to surface constraints so we can be aligned in the playbook and the redline response. Posting here to keep the thread intact.

1) Hosted (standard Redwood API):
   - Default: transient routing may hit non-US edge regions for operational reasons (network failover, regional capacity burst). We typically see these events as short (< 6 hours) but don't have a hard SLA today.
   - We can commit to a documented notification flow and preserve logs/telemetry to show which requests were routed.

2) Dedicated / Private customers:
   - For Dedicated pools and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments we can implement configuration controls that prevent cross-region routing and enforce a transient-window cap (we currently ship a 72-hour default transient buffer for failover testing).
   - Important: enforcing tighter windows (48h) is possible, but operationally it requires an agreed runbook and a short ops maintenance SLA (we may need an approval path for emergency capacity increases).

3) Technical implications:
   - KV cache and prefix caches: a transient failover may require cache warming; during the window, some traffic may be routed to compatible model variants in a neighboring region.
   - KMS / key paths: cross-region telemetry does not expose customer plaintext; KMS keys remain region-tagged unless customer opts into cross-region KMS replication.

Suggested compromise to offer Wintergreen:
   - Offer a contractual commitment for Hosted customers: notification within 1 hour of an event, post-mortem within 72 hours, retained routing logs for 180 days.
   - For customers on Dedicated or Private: offer a contractual 48-hour transient window option (addendum) gated by an operational change approval and a short onboarding checklist (ops contacts, emergency capacity phone number).

I'll attach a short tech appendix to the playbook that describes these constraints (will send to Eve).

—Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Asha / team — thanks for your patience. Attached is a short packet for your review: 1) Conditional_Egress_Playbook_v1.pdf (one-page playbook + appendix), 2) redline summary (DPA_redline_comments.xlsx with our counter-suggested language called out), and 3) the SOW we discussed.

Key points (TL;DR):
- Hosted customers: we cannot contractually guarantee a 48-hour maximum for all hosted events today. Our standard commitment: same-hour notification where feasible, 72-hour post-mortem, and 180-day routing log retention. We will include explicit telemetry access and a notification SLA in the DPA for Wintergreen if you accept hosted with those guardrails.
- Dedicated / Private option: we can offer a 48-hour contractual transient window as an addendum to the DPA for Dedicated pools or Private deployments. This requires: a short ops onboarding checklist (contacts, escalation path), a one-week staged cutover for enforcement, and an operational approval flow for emergency capacity expansion.
- Subprocessors: the attached playbook appendix lists the subprocessors that may see transient telemetry and their regions. If you want, Marissa and I can produce a signed subprocessor roster annex for the DPA.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached packet and the counter-language in the spreadsheet.
2) If the Dedicated/Private 48-hour addendum is required, confirm and we'll provide a short ops checklist and a target timeline (7–10 business days) to finalize the configuration and contract addendum.
3) Would you be available for a 30-minute call on Tuesday 7/19 or Wednesday 7/20 to walk through the playbook and close open redlines? Matt — happy to lock a DocuSign window if you send preferred dates.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Conditional_Egress_Playbook_v1.pdf, DPA_redline_comments.xlsx (with our counters), Wintergreen_SOW_v3.pdf
